declarations.description:
Broker user actions in a normalized way which is abstracted from xAPI
but yet mirrors much of that structure and data needs.

Normalization: listen() (once per page) turns every `user-engagement`
and `learner-progress-import` event that reaches the window into one xAPI
statement (see ./xapi.js) and hands it to every subscriber registered
with subscribe(fn). Events that already carry `detail.statement` keep it;
older or third party events are converted from their loose fields, and
events marked `xapi: false` are not learner records.

`question-element-state` is not a learner record source: every question
element sends its own answered statement on user-engagement, and the state
event (still fired for question-stack and page logic) only repeated it.
Subscribers get ({ statement, element, eventName, detail, imported }).
declarations.name: UserActionBroker

members.name: subscribe
members.description:
Register a function called with each normalized statement. Returns a
function that removes it.

members.name: listen
members.description:
Start normalizing learner events that reach target (default window).
Safe to call more than once.

members.name: normalize
members.description:
One xAPI statement for an event detail, or null when it is not a
learner record.

members.name: valid
members.description: See if this is a valid event

members.name: fire
members.description: Fire the action for the user engagement broker.

declarations.name: XAPI_VERBS
declarations.default: { answered: "http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/answered", attempted: "http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/attempted", completed: "http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/completed", experienced: "http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/experienced", progressed: "http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/progressed", interacted: "http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/interacted", }
declarations.description:
ADL verb IRIs used by HAX elements. Each has one meaning:
  experienced  saw or opened something; no judgment, no progress
  interacted   manipulated something with no right answer
  answered     gave a response (judged or not, see result.success)
  progressed   finished one step of a multi-part activity
  attempted    began an attempt
  completed    finished the whole activity
Pass and fail are result.success on the answered / completed statement;
statements imported from elsewhere may still use other ADL verbs.

declarations.name: authoredResource
declarations.description:
The `resource` attribute an element had in its markup when it connected
(authored, or saved by HAX), or "" when it had none. SchemaBehaviors
(@haxtheweb/schema-behaviors) records it as `_xapiAuthoredResource` before
its first update, which is when it generates a random `resource` for
elements without one; a generated value changes on every page load, so it
is never used here. Elements without SchemaBehaviors can set
`_xapiAuthoredResource` themselves (read the attribute in
connectedCallback before anything can write it).

declarations.name: fillInItem
declarations.description:
One fill-in / long-fill-in item of free text. The spec has no escape for
the "[,]" delimiter, so it (and "[.]") is reduced to its middle character.
A characterstring parameter ({case_matters=...}, {lang=...}) is only
recognised at the start of an item, so text that itself starts with "{"
gets the item level {lang=<tag>} parameter the spec defines in front of
it; readers drop that prefix and read the text after it unchanged.
